case_scope.source_excerpt:
Let $m\ge1$ and $d\ge1$ be integers, let $q_1,\ldots,q_m\in\mathbb R^d$, and let $a_1,\ldots,a_m\in\mathbb R$. Put

$$\Delta_m=\{\theta\in\mathbb R^m:\theta_i\ge0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m\theta_i=1\},\qquad P:=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m\theta_iq_i:\theta\in\Delta_m\right\}.$$

Thus $P$ is the finite convex hull of the listed points, defined here as their convex combinations.

For $x\in P$ let $\Theta_x=\{\theta\in\Delta_m:\sum_i\theta_iq_i=x\}$ and define

$$f_{\rm mix}(x)=\min_{\theta\in\Theta_x}\sum_{i=1}^m\theta_i a_i;$$

set $f_{\rm mix}(x)=+\infty$ for $x\notin P$. Then every minimum is attained; $f_{\rm mix}$ is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex; and it is pointwise greatest among convex functions $h:\mathbb R^d\to\overline{\mathbb R}$ satisfying $h(q_i)\le a_i$ for every $i$. Consequently $f_{\rm mix}=f_{\rm mix}^{**}$. If $p\in\partial f_{\rm mix}(x)$ and $\theta$ is any minimizing mixture for $x$, then every $i$ with $\theta_i>0$ satisfies

$$a_i=\langle p,q_i\rangle-f_{\rm mix}^*(p).$$

Thus all occupied data points $(q_i,a_i)$ lie on one supporting affine hyperplane. The assertion is finite-dimensional and makes no claim about infinite families.
case_scope.case_interpretation: m>=1 excludes an empty generator list; infeasible coordinate fibers receive+infinity.

case_scope.source_excerpt: Assume the strict-reference representation conclusion of the draft supplier [[thm-tdmath-additive-entropy-representation]] for its nonempty state set $X$ and stated comparison hypotheses. Let $d\ge1$ and $m\ge1$ be integers, and take a finite list of distinct states $s_1,\ldots,s_m\in X$. Let $q_1,\ldots,q_m\in\mathbb R^d$ and set $a_i:=S(s_i)$ for $1\le i\le m$. Let $e_s$ be the unit-state compound defined in [[def-tdmath-tagged-scalable-compound]]; it is a mass-one point mass by [[lem-tdmath-compound-mass-well-defined]]. For $\theta\in\Delta_m$, put $M_\theta=\sum_i\theta_i e_{s_i}$ and set $V(\theta):=\sum_i\theta_iS(s_i)$. Suppose a map $\chi:\{M_\theta:\theta\in\Delta_m\}\to\mathbb R^d$ satisfies $\chi(M_\theta)=\sum_i\theta_iq_i$ for every $\theta\in\Delta_m$. For each $x\in\mathbb R^d$, define the value to be $+\infty$ if no $\theta\in\Delta_m$ has coordinate $x$. Then the minimum represented value among those finite mixtures, with that empty-feasible-set convention, is exactly the finite-mixture envelope $f_{\rm mix}(x)$ of [[thm-tdmath-finite-mixture-envelope]], with all its attainment, convexity, lower-semicontinuity, biconjugation, and supporting-face conclusions. This is the complete conditional transfer under the representation conclusion and affine coordinate assignment; the supplier definition and mass-one fact are provided locally.

Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]]. Assume the filtered probability space, Brownian increment hypothesis, and initial data of [[def-tdmath-ornstein-uhlenbeck-equation]], including $\mathbb E X_0^2<\infty$ and future increments independent of $\mathcal F_0$. For $\gamma,\sigma>0$, on every finite time interval the process
$$X_t=e^{-\gamma t}X_0+\sigma e^{-\gamma t}\int_0^t e^{\gamma s}\,dB_s$$
has a continuous adapted version, solves the stated Ornstein–Uhlenbeck integral equation, and is the unique continuous solution driven by the same $(X_0,B)$. Put $V=\sigma^2/(2\gamma)$. For $0\le s<t$, its transition law conditional on $\mathcal F_s$ is normal with mean $e^{-\gamma(t-s)}X_s$ and variance $V(1-e^{-2\gamma(t-s)})$. Consequently
$$\mathbb E X_t=e^{-\gamma t}\mathbb E X_0,\qquad\operatorname{Var}(X_t)=e^{-2\gamma t}\operatorname{Var}(X_0)+V(1-e^{-2\gamma t}).$$
From any such initial law, $X_t$ converges in distribution to $N(0,V)$. If $X_0\sim N(0,V)$ and is independent of future Brownian increments, the process is stationary Gaussian with covariance $C(\tau)=Ve^{-\gamma|\tau|}$, and its transition kernel satisfies detailed balance with the $N(0,V)$ density. $$S(\omega)=\frac{V\gamma}{\pi(\gamma^2+\omega^2)},\qquad\operatorname{Var}\!\left(\frac1T\int_0^T X_t\,dt\right)\le\frac{2V}{\gamma T}.$$
